articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Proposed heavyweight super fight moves step closer to being in USA over UK
articles.summary: Turki Alalshikh, who is organising the all-British bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua, now prefers the clash to be in the USA; Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says the contract they signed was for a fight in the UK
articles.body:
Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has revealed that Turki Alalshikh, who is organising the all-British bout, now prefers the clash to be in the USA.

Alalshikh previously said that he wants the fight to take place at a time that works for a global audience and would hold talks with the Mayor of London, Sir Sadiq Khan, over a later-than-usual start time.

However, Sky Sports News revealed earlier in the week that Brent Council are yet to be contacted about extending the curfew at Wembley Stadium to allow a 2am ring walk.

Speaking to DAZN ahead of Joshua's warm-up fight with Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia on Saturday, Hearn said: "We've been told in the last 24 hours that [a fight in America] is what they want.

"That doesn't tally up with the contract that we signed. Until we're happy, we expect every point of that contract to be followed. I feel like this fight should be taking place in the UK.

"Anthony Joshua insisted that the contract stated that the fight must be in the UK.

"If they want to change the contract, then we have to renegotiate the contract. Which, by the way, is not a problem. But it's a conversation we have to have."

Fury: I got through my test, what about AJ?

Fury remains unconvinced that Joshua will agree to the fight and questioned whether his rival has the "guts" to face him.

The 37-year-old, speaking after his seventh-round stoppage of Mariusz Wach in a non-televised bout in Thailand on Friday, referenced Joshua opting not to get in the ring with him after his victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

Fury said: "I got through my test. Let's see if [Joshua] gets through his test. The biggest test of it all is how big his balls are. I think he's a big s***house.

"In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me. Let's see if he ever does. I'm not convinced.

"I'll regroup. Hopefully the next big fight is signed next week, and we head wherever we're going to head.

"Is it gonna be in Vegas? Is it gonna be in New York? Is it gonna be in Ireland? Is it gonna be in London? Who knows, Belfast maybe? It might even be here in Pattaya, Thailand!"

articles.title: Hamzah Sheeraz escapes with narrow points win, while Josh Kelly overcomes horror gash to his nose in Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Hamzah Sheeraz is forced to go the distance against unheralded Simon Zachenhuber, with Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez in his sights while Josh Kelly left the ring covered in blood after beating Irishman Caoimhin Agyarko
articles.body:
Londoner Sheeraz, who sealed his first world title with a second-round stoppage win against Alem Begic to claim the vacant WBO super-middleweight crown in Egypt, defeated Germany's Simon Zachenhuber.

After a 12-round fight that ended with boos around the arena the judges returned scores of 114-114, 115-113 and 116-112, in favour of Sheeraz, who posed with Jacob Bank in the ring following his win.

"I am a champion in the division. I'm sure people are champing at the bit after [my] performance," said Sheeraz, who said he would be sat ringside on October 31 to watch Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez challenge for Christian Mbilli's WBC belt.

"I got the win, that's all that matters. I could make a million excuses. I'll be better in the next fight.

"I need a step up now, someone who will mentally present a challenge. I was switching off at times, I was too comfortable when I didn't have a threat in front of me."

Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose as he secured a unanimous points win against Irishman Caoimhin Agyarko in an IBF Light-Middleweight title fight in Saudi Arabia.

Nicknamed 'Pretty Boy', Kelly was left bloodied as the pair clashed heads in the 11th round with the Brit's face left a mess.

But he did enough to get the win with scorecards of 115-112, 115-112, 114-113.

"I told Caoimhin, don't take it as a loss, take it as a learning. If he wants it bad enough, he will bounce back," said Kelly.

Agyarko said: "I thought I won it, but if it's not good enough for the judges, I accept that. I'm heartbroken, I wanted to make history. Josh Kelly is a class act, but I think he underestimated me a bit, there.

"Listen, it will come. I will be the first Black Irish world champion, there's no doubt about that."

After the bout, Kelly said he wants to face unified 154-pound champion Jaron 'Boots' Ennis.

Promoter Eddie Hearn, who represents both Kelly and Ennis, said a clash between the two in the States is now a real option.

"He's had a defence of the title and before that mandatory comes again, really you want to be looking at those big money fights and trying to roll the dice," Hearn said.

"I think that comes with 'Boots' Ennis. If I'm Josh Kelly I'm looking at the big payday out in America against 'Boots' Ennis. It's a three-belt unification fight. [WBC champion] Sebastian Fundora, all those guys."

articles.title: Errol Spence Jr announces retirement after Tim Tszyu claims biggest career win in Sydney
articles.summary: Tim Tszyu beat Errol Spence Jr 118-110 117-111 117-111 in their middleweight showdown at a sold-out Afterpay Arena; Spence, the former unified welterweight champion, confirmed his retirement in the ring after only the second defeat of his career
articles.body:
The 36-year-old Texan, one of the finest American fighters of his generation, confirmed in the ring at a sold-out Afterpay Arena that he will not fight again after only the second defeat of his career.

Spence had not fought since his 2023 defeat to Terence Crawford and jumped two divisions to meet Tszyu at middleweight after three years away. Crawford, recently retired as the sport's pound-for-pound king, watched from ringside as his old rival gave everything one final time.

As for Tszyu, the former WBO super welterweight champion arrived rebranded as "the Phoenix" and knowing his career could not absorb another setback after three world-title defeats in America, twice to Sebastian Fundora and once to Bakhram Murtazaliev. This was his first fight under new trainer Jeff Fenech, and it will live long in both men's memories.

Tszyu snapped Spence's head back with clean right hands inside the opening round, but the American's class showed early. He was the busier man through the first half, investing heavily to the body and at times doubling Tszyu's output, even if his balance never looked fully trustworthy following the long layoff.

The pattern turned in the seventh. Spence simply could not time the right hand coming back at him, and Tszyu began landing it flush and often, coming close to putting the American down for only the third time in his career.

Spence found a big left in the 10th and, told bluntly by trainer Ronnie Shields that he was not doing enough, emptied himself into a defiant 11th.

Tszyu dominated the last in keeping with most of the fight, though, punctuating the night with a right hand that sent Spence stumbling back into the corner pad and the three cards reflected his second-half control, scoring the contest 118-110 117-111 117-111 in the home favourite's favour.

Tszyu continues family legacy as Spence bows out to applause

Tszyu admitted afterwards that he was relieved to pick up the victory and considers it the highlight of his career so far.

"I had sleepless nights, what am I gonna feel like facing a legend like that?" the 31-year-old admitted afterwards. "I understand why he's one of the greats.

"Two greats I'm trying to replicate, Kostya Tszyu and Jeff Fenech. If I can get half as great as them, I'll be a great man.

"Beating a great like Errol Spence tops any world title for me. The Tszyu legacy is continuing. I told you so."

The win preserved a family streak that now stretches 31 years. Tszyu is 26-0 in Australia, matching the perfect home records of his Hall of Fame father Kostya and younger brother Nikita for a combined 56-0 on home soil.

Tszyu, now 28-3, confirmed middleweight is his new home and named WBA champion Erislandy Lara as a possible next opponent with Crawford's presence in the building a reminder that another big American night, and another world-title shot, are suddenly back on the table.

The Sydney crowd applauded Spence as he confirmed his decision, closing a professional career of almost 14 years that followed a 135-12 amateur record and one that survived a near-fatal car crash along the way.

"I've got my faculties intact. My money is good, it's working for itself. Everything's good," he said. "I've got a beautiful family. I thank God that I'm gracious enough to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family still by my side.

"I asked a lot of questions of myself. Now it's time to go home with my family and start a new life."

He retires at 28-2 with 22 knockouts, a former unified champion whose wins over Kell Brook, Shawn Porter and Yordenis Ugas collected three of the four major belts at welterweight.

articles.title: Tyson Fury can't pull out of Anthony Joshua fight despite his 'shouting and screaming', says Eddie Hearn
articles.summary: Tyson Fury had cast doubts over the Anthony Joshua fight after claiming on social media his British rival has asked for "more money", labelling him and his team "cowards"; Fury and Joshua have been negotiating a long-awaited heavyweight clash for a proposed date in November
articles.body:
Fury claimed on Friday that the proposed fight is in serious doubt after Joshua supposedly asked for "more money", labelling him and his team "cowards".

But Hearn, who represents Joshua, is confident the fight will still go ahead.

"We've signed the contract, we're waiting for a date. You saw Tyson Fury shouting and screaming - there's nothing to shout and scream about, the fight's done," he told DAZN .

"The fight's signed. No-one can pull out of the fight. You can't just pull out of a contract.

"There's no suggestion that the fight's not happening, no-one can stop this fight from happening. The only way it can stop from happening is if they actually breach the contract."

Fury and Joshua have been in talks about staging the proposed all-British bout in November, with Madison Square Garden in New York as the likely location.

Hearn said the original fight contract stipulated that the bout would be staged in the UK, but Saudi organisers Sela are pushing for a move to the United States.

"We know everybody and his dog involved in the fight wants to do the fight in America. We don't," added Hearn.

"We've told Sela and the team if you want to do it in America, these are the terms that we can move forward with. But we'd rather not please."

Joshua and Fury were unable to agree terms in 2021 and fight plans fell apart after a US judge ruled Fury had to face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy fight instead.

articles.title: Caroline Dubois vs Amelia Moore: Win for Briton keeps Alycia Baumgardner showdown in picture
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois coasts to victory over Amelia Moore in Birmingham to defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles and stay on course for a blockbuster meeting with Alycia Baumgardner.
articles.body:
Caroline Dubois coasted to victory over Amelia Moore to defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles and stay on course for a blockbuster meeting with unified super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner in 2027.

Dubois dominated the fight at BP Pulse Arenain Birmingham and knocked Moore down in the fifth round but was unable to find the decisive blow against the dogged American.

The British fighter won on unanimous judges' decision, 99-90 99-90 98-91 ahead on the scorecards.

Dubois was heavy favourite for this fight and never looked less than in control, although her reliance on power and presence rather than speed ensured it went the distance to a long, inevitable conclusion.

She sent Moore to the canvas with a booming left in round five, but Moore got straight back up and was instead moved around the ring by Dubois like a cat playing with a mouse.

After the fight, Dubois had a war of words with the watching Baumgardner, who accused the Briton of "tightening up" and being "tired".

In just her fifth professional fight, Moore - who has two American national championships from a respectable amateur career - showed admirable guts, but lacked the quality to trouble her foe.

It was clear that Dubois has boxed 70 more professional rounds than Moore, and she made light of being four inches shorter to avoid any danger.

Now it is anticipated that Dubois, now unbeaten in 15 professional fights with 14 wins, will face Baumgardner next year - should the American beat Elif Nur Turhan in November.

Dubois and Baumgardner - who both gave separate media conferences promoting their respective upcoming fights in Birmingham on Thursday - have been sniping at each other for a year.

And it continued ringside post-fight, with Baumgardner present for what she called a "scouting mission" on Dubois on Saturday night.

Dubois' new MVP-curated personality - brash and self-confident - was on display as she called out Baumgardner for stepping into "my division - I am the best here", in an expletive-infused exchange.

She has also made changes outside ring, including a shock decision to switch trainer.

Dubois dropped Shane McGuigan in London, who helped guide her to two world titles in the lightweight division, and has opted to make the move to Los Angeles to work with renowned US trainer Manny Robles as she aims to take her career to the next level.

Baumgardner has said she "absolutely" wants to fight Dubois, and if the 32-year-old successfully steps up to lightweight and beats IBF champion Turhan in Texas on 8 November, then they should headline another MVP showcase of women's boxing.

Earlier on the undercard, Terri Harper - who lost on points to Dubois in April - began her rebuild with a comprehensive victory against Miranda Reyes which she described as "one of the best performances of my career".

Harper considered retirement after losing to Sandy Ryan in 2024, but had no such thoughts after defeat by Dubois.

And she stepped up to welterweight to take on Reyes, knowing this was a must-win bout to maintain her career as a top-rated fighter.

Harper bounced into the ring with bright yellow gloves, and there was nothing mellow as she continued that energy into the first round - holding the centre of the ring for the majority and landing some good body shots on Reyes.

She then upped her game and brought an early close at the start of the second round, dropping Reyes twice in short order.

A flurry of body shots was followed by a short left hook to down the Houston fighter, and the referee called it off 47 seconds into the second round to the delight of Harper's similarly yellow-attired corner.

"One of the best performances of my career, I'm very happy with that," Harper said. "You can't get rid of me this easily!

"I am excited for what's next. It's way too early [to say goodbye] - I've got a lot to give yet."

It is the seventh knockout win of Harper's career from 17 victories in 22 bouts, and she will now look up again after a timely reminder of her capabilities.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley: Heavyweight world title rematch to take place in London
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois will defend his WBO heavyweight world title against the man he dethroned Fabio Wardley in a rematch on 17 October in London.
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois will defend his WBO heavyweight world title against former champion Fabio Wardley in a highly anticipated rematch on 17 October at London's O2 Arena.

Londoner Dubois, 28, dethroned Wardley with an 11th-round stoppage in a thrilling all-British showdown in Manchester in May to become a two-time world champion.

It was announced during Saturday's undercard of Moses Itauma's IBF heavyweight world title fight with Filip Hrgovic, with Dubois and Wardley facing off in the ring.

Dubois said he is predicting a "dominant victory" before adding: "Let's get it on. It's just a war.

"When you get in the water, you're going to get wet. We will see. Give me some of that face-to-face - boy."

The first meeting lived up to its billing, with two of the division's biggest punchers producing a dramatic fight that showcased the power of both men.

Wardley dropped Dubois twice early in the contest, but a bloodied Wardley absorbed heavy punishment before the referee stopped the bout.

It was the first defeat of the 31-year-old's professional career in his 22nd bout.

"It didn't take long at all [to agree]. The O2 is like a home away from home for me," Fabio Wardley said on DAZN.

"Looking forward to getting straight back into it. Going to be a rematch and going to be revenge.

"We came into the fight with all the confidence in the world, but adjustments needed to be made."

The Ipswich fighter's rise through the sport has been remarkable. Having only taken up boxing at the age of 19, he progressed through the unlicensed white-collar scene before reaching the top of the heavyweight division.

Dubois, meanwhile, has experienced the full spectrum of boxing's highs and lows.

The 26-fight veteran has suffered three defeats during his career but rebuilt himself to claim world honours twice, with his victory over Wardley marking the latest chapter in his comeback story.

The winner of the rematch could be in line for a blockbuster fight next summer against fellow Briton Itauma, provided the heavyweight prospect secures a world title of his own.

The winner of the contest between Itauma and Hrgovic will be required to face mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez.

Should Itauma - who is aiming to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion in history after Mike Tyson - come through both fights, promoter Frank Warren has suggested a potential Wembley Stadium clash with the winner of Dubois-Wardley II next summer.

The heavyweight division remains fragmented following Oleksandr Usyk's decision to vacate his titles. Russian Murat Gassiev currently holds the WBA belt, while Germany's Agit Kabayel is the WBC champion.

articles.title: Caroline Dubois beats Amelia Moore before clashing with Alycia Baumgardner ahead of potential super-fight
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois retains WBC and WBO lightweight world titles with dominant victory over Amelia Moore in MVPW-06 co-main event; Terri Harper produces second-round stoppage against Miranda Reyes while Reina Tellez defeats Jessica Barry
articles.body:
The Londoner was rarely troubled throughout a commanding performance to claim a 99-90, 99-90, 98-91 unanimous decision victory and retain her WBC and WBO lightweight world titles in the co-main event at MVPW-06 in Birmingham on Saturday.

Dubois subsequently engaged in a war of words with former undisputed champion Baumgardner, who steps into the same division when she fights Elif Nur Turhan on November 8.

Baumgardner has made her presence felt all week in Birmingham, quizzing former rival Mikaela Mayer at her final press conference while reiterating her belief Dubois is not yet at her level.

"That was a lacklustre performance," said Baumgardner. "You gotta tighten up baby girl. You was tired baby. You was real tired. I'm gonna show you what a champ do Undisputed champ at that. I'm at lightweight now."

Dubois replied: "I've been calling for this for a long time. After the last fight I said move up and fight that bum? What's happened to Amanda Serrano? What happened to Katie Taylor?

"What happened to Claressa Shields? You haven't got anything you've asked for. I got what I asked for. You are moving up to my division. I'm the best in the division and you know it. I'm 25 and I'm better than you.

" I love that. Keep that energy. If you get through Elif Nur Turhan, me and you there's no denying it. Everything I've asked for has happened. I'm knocking this bum out, you'd better believe it."

Dubois asserted herself on the front foot early with a lightning flurry of body shots in the first round, taking control of the distancing in the face of Moore's lengthy reach.

The Londoner sought to find her range in the second against the counter-shot approach of Moore, closing the two minutes with an overhand right to the head of her opponent.

Dubois would continue to control the tempo of the fight in rounds three and four, turning to the body of the well-conditioned Moore, who was struggling to find her target against the sharp movement of her opponent.

A defining flashpoint came in round five when Dubois found the breakthrough with a knockdown seemingly caused by Moore losing her balance more so than the champion's power on this occasion.

Still, Dubois worked to capitalise as she resumed with a fierce attack capped by a right hook.

Dubois landed again with sharp hooks to the head of Moore in round seven, before breaching the American's guard with a crisp straight left.

Blood began to trickly from the nose of Moore in round eight as Dubois sustained her dominance despite a late front foot attack from the challenge in the ninth.

Moore was in the wars again in the final round as she sustained a cut during an accidental clash of heads.

Terri Harper marked her return to the ring in style as she produced a clinical second-round stoppage victory against Houston's Miranda Reyes in her first fight since April's defeat to Dubois.

The Doncaster fighter initially floored Reyes with a beautifully-timed left hand, from which the American continued to look unsteady as she returned to her feet.It didn't take much longer for Harper to finish it, a flurry of hooks being followed by a punishing right hand to put Reyes down for a second time. Reyes returned to her feet yet again, only for the referee to rightly wave off the contest.

"One of the best performances of my career. I'm very happy with that," Harper told Sky Sports .

"It's good to do that to build the fight up, but you can't get rid of me that easily!

"This journey that I've been on through my boxing career, the highs and lows - I'm just grateful for MVP bringing me back so soon after my last fight.

Reina Tellez delivered a ferocious performance to out-gun Jessica Barry in a thrilling points victory for the American fighter.

Tellez, who notably fought the great Amanda Serrano at 15 days' notice in January, landed the cleaner, more eye-catching shots in a straight fire fight to claim a 96-94 win.

"I feel a little bit of ring rust, but overall I feel great, Tellez told Sky Sports .

"There were things that happened in the fight, but that's what comes with experience. I'm grateful for the platform and opportunity I've been given.

"She showed a lot of heart. A good opponent with a different style. I give her respect. But overall I dominated the fight."

The 23-year-old controlled the exchanges for much of the first four rounds, fast hands meeting accuracy and power to find the head of Barry time and time again.

Barry continued to come forward, though, and came back into the fight in the fifth round as she landed a flush upper-cut.

An undeterred Tellez was deducted a point in round six for a low blow before launching back into an assault and landing a brutal right hand in the eighth to trouble Barry.

Barry showed her toughness and continued to meet fire with fire, but it would be Tellez whose output and full-blooded attacks that prevailed.

Tysie Gallagher celebrated her MVP debut with a points victory over Chicago's Brandi Robinson to improve to 11-2 as a professional.

"I'm not particularly happy about the performance, couldn't really get going, first one back, no excuses. I'll be back 100 per cent next time."

articles.title: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley rematch announced to take place in October with The O2 in London set to host heavyweight showdown
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois stopped Fabio Wardley in the 11th round of a Fight of the Year contender in Manchester in May to win the WBO heavyweight title; the rematch takes place at The O2 in London on Saturday October 17
articles.body:
Dubois climbed off the canvas twice at the Co-op Live Arena in May – dropped inside the opening seconds and down again on one knee in the third – before grinding Wardley into a stoppage with the defending champion's nose gashed, his eye swollen and referee Howard Foster finally stepping in early in the 11th with Wardley still refusing to go down.

The rematch honours the clause promoter Frank Warren confirmed in the ring in Manchester, moments after one of the great modern British heavyweight fights .

Victory made Dubois a two-time world heavyweight champion, adding the WBO belt to the IBF title he previously held and defended with his knockout of Anthony Joshua at Wembley, and it ended Wardley's reign at a first defence.

The O2 is a fitting stage for the rematch too, as it was there last October that Wardley announced himself at world level, coming back from the brink to stop Joseph Parker in the 11th round for the interim WBO title.

He was then elevated to full champion when Oleksandr Usyk vacated the belt, a remarkable rise for a man who began in white-collar boxing.

Warren: You're going to see a brilliant fight

Frank Warren, who promotes Dubois and Wardley, announced the rematch in the ring at the The O2 ahead of Moses Itauma's heavyweight title fight against Filip Hrgovic.

Warren said: "October 17 here at the O2, here in London, the rematch. One of the greatest heavyweight fights we've seen in years.

"This is going to be the rematch of the champion here, Daniel Dubois, against the former champion, Fabio Wardley.

"You are going to see a brilliant fight on October 17. Be here for it."

Facing Wardley in the ring, Dubois predicted: "Another dominant victory and amazing performance. I can't wait. Let's get it on.

"It's just a war. When you get in the water, you're going to get wet. I love every bit of it. I can't wait for it."

Wardley replied: "We came into that fight with all the confidence in the world but adjustments need to be made.

"I've proven I'm adaptable and I can change, and that's what we need to do for this fight."

articles.title: Anthony Cacace-Nick Ball: Belfast world title showdown set for December
articles.summary: Anthony Cacace will make the first defence of his WBA super-featherweight world title against Nick Ball at The 02 in Belfast on 19 December.
articles.body:
Anthony Cacace will make the first defence of his WBA super-featherweight world title against Nick Ball at The 02 in Belfast on 19 December.

The 37-year-old from Belfast won the title in March with a points victory of James 'Jazza' Dickens in Dublin and will face another Liverpool native in former featherweight champion Ball.

Cacace's last fight in his home city occurred in May 2023 with a defence of the IBO belt against Damian Wrzesinski on the undercard of Luis Alberto Lopez's featherweight title victory over Michael Conlan.

Since then, he has won and then relinquished the IBF title before becoming a two-time champion at the weight with victory over Dickens which saw his record improve to 25 wins with one loss.

"Nick's a great fighter, ex-world champion, so I expect a good scrap. He's a hard man, so let's do it," Cacace told DAZN.

"I'll fight with him, I'll box him - whatever way he wants, so we'll see what happens on the night. I'm really looking forward to it.

"Belfast around Christmas time is going to be jumping, so I'm looking forward to it."

Ball is coming off his first career defeat when stopped in the final round by Brandon Figueroa in a defence of the WBA featherweight title in February.

The Liverpudlian won the title in 2024 with a points verdict over Raymond Ford, three months after his first bid for world honours ended in a draw against then-WBC champion Rey Vargas.

He fought on the same Belfast card as Cacace in 2023 when stopping Ludumo Lamati, who suffered a stroke in the ring but has since recovered , and is relishing the chance to become a two-weight champion.

"It's a massive opportunity at a new weight," said Ball, whose record is 23-1-1.

"He's a solid champion, so it's going to be a good fight. I'll be coming, he'll be coming, so it's going to be a good one."

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer v Chantelle Cameron: Brit wins to become unified light-middleweight champion
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron produced one of the finest displays of her career to beat Mikaela Mayer and add the WBA and WBC light middleweight titles to her WBO belt.
articles.body:
Chantelle Cameron produced one of the finest displays of her career to beat Mikaela Mayer and add the WBA and WBC light middleweight titles to her WBO belt.

An engrossing encounter was narrowly won by the British fighter by unanimous decision - 97-93 on two scorecards and 96-94 on the other.

American Mayer disagreed with the decision, claiming she "outboxed" Cameron – leading to an angry exchange of words in the ring.

The possibility of a rematch was also floated, with Mayer also suggesting Cameron had benefited from home advantage – to the champion's chagrin, as she said "talk is cheap".

It means Cameron remains unbeaten since her second fight with Katie Taylor in 2023, and with 23 victories in 24 professional encounters.

And this was one of her best displays. These fighters were evenly matched in every metric – from punch rate to height and weight, even hairstyle.

But Cameron won out thanks to her unrelenting pressure, which never allowed the usually adaptable Mayer to figure out a winning gameplan.

Mayer was the more imposing figure early on, but Cameron played counterpuncher until she could get onto the front foot.

Cameron forced Mayer against the ropes in round four, and again at the start of the fifth. Increasingly confident to take the initiative, she was roared on by a partisan but disappointingly small home crowd.

Mayer was unable to get in behind her jab for long periods and was bleeding and breathing heavily by round six.

The home favourite was cut in the final rounds but pushed through and was lifted shoulder high by her team before her biggest win since beating Taylor in Dublin three years ago was announced.

For three-weight world champion Mayer, this is the third defeat of her 25-fight career and costs her the WBA and WBC belts, which Cameron now puts with her WBO title.

From influencers to queens of women's boxing - five years of MVP

Watch every Born to Brawl episode Published 28 April 2024

When this event was announced, it was the prime event of the August bank holiday weekend in British boxing.

However, the elevation of Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgovic to a world title fight left this big-ticket event feeling rather undeservedly like a support act.

That was reflected in the crowd, with scores of empty seats around the arena as the main undercard began. At a generous estimate, BP Pulse Arena was half-full when the fighters made their ring walks for the main event.

Mayer and Cameron did their best to bring the big fight feeling in the build-up. Previously cordial relations boiled over on Friday as they butted heads at Friday's weigh-in at BP Pulse Arena.

Cameron shoved her head into the American, who pushed back, before they exchanged insults side by side.

On fight night, Mayer played up her away status by entering the ring to American Woman by Lenny Kravitz. She also wore a black durag over her trademark blonde hair, before removing it to show tight dreadlocks – the same style as Cameron.

However, her moxie was eventually worn down by Cameron, with a big right to the chin in round seven the most notable of blows.

This fight headlined the event marking the fifth anniversary of Most Valuable Promotions (MVP), the promoters fronted by Jake Paul who, since 2021, have moved from YouTuber fights to leading the way for women's boxing in the UK.

Paul, influencer and co-founder of MVP, was in the house. He headlined on 29 August 2021, beating MMA fighter Tyron Woodley, but was in a watching brief here.

MVP's next women's boxing arena event will take place in November in Texas.

It will be headlined by unified super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner, with the American stepping up to lightweight to face Elif Nur Turhan – on her way to a potential 2027 showdown versus Caroline Dubois.

World championship fights on the undercard will include featherweight champion Tiara Brown defending against former undisputed champion Ellie Scotney, and super bantamweight champion Skye Nicolson against three-time, two-division champion Miyo Yoshida.

The next fight is particularly important for Cameron, after her first fight at BP Pulse Arena since November 2024 – and her first since her much-lauded move to MVP.

MVP have plenty of options they could introduce from their stable. IBF light middleweight champion Oshae Jones seems the logical next step; or IBF, WBO and The Ring middleweight belt holder Tammara Thibeault of Canada.

Cameron regularly laments that she has not had the chances her talent deserves since her blockbuster double header against Taylor in 2023.

Three years on, she will want fights of that level – especially after Saturday night's result.

articles.title: Chantelle Cameron defeats Mikaela Mayer in epic to emphasise place among boxing greats
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron becomes WBA, WBC and WBO super-welterweight champion of the world after victory over Mikaela  Mayer in main event at MVPW-06 in Birmingham.
articles.body:
What had been billed as a fight of the year contender did not disappoint as the pound-for-pound superstars fought at a frenetic, unrelenting pace in a bruising main event.

It would be Cameron who emerged victorious as she edged a tight-knit contest 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 on the judges' scorecards, further glossing a stellar resume that already honours her as the only woman to ever defeat the great Katie Taylor in her professional career.

"I just wanted to play with [Mayer]," said Cameron. "If you're going to say you'll stop me, beat me easily... talk is so cheap, and I showed that tonight. Don't talk too much game - you've got to back it.

"I want to do this again. It's up to Mikaela, but I want to do three-minute rounds.

"I'll speak to my team and see if Mikaela wants it, but - [to Mayer] - didn't you say you were going to beat me so bad that I wasn't going to want a rematch?"

Tempers had flared just a day earlier when Mayer and Cameron needed to be split by security after a physical altercation and fierce war of words at their weigh-in.

It had been a drastic change of tempo to a largely-relaxed build-up between the two pound-for-pound stars, a furious Cameron having promised to "smash her head in".

The tone followed suit from the opening bell as the pair went toe-to-toe in a classic culminating in another volley of insults after the final bell as Mayer suggested she had won the fight.

"I did beat you Chantelle. You are lucky in your little back yard," said Mayer.

"You can have your re-match. Three-minute f****** rounds. If you want to vacate your WBC belt you can do that. It's your prerogative now. I'll just kick your ass even harder.

"But it won't be here. It won't be in the UK. If you want to come to the US you can.

"I outboxed you. I'll go back and rewatched it and give an honest evaluation, but I just beat you.

"If the public says I'm wrong you can have that... my initial feeling is I outboxed her."

The bad blood of Friday's weigh-in flared at the end of the first round when the two bumped shoulders before squaring up on their way back to the corner.

Before then Mayer had sought to make a front foot attack, Cameron though timing her counter shot perfectly to land a left hook.

Cameron continued to look the more dangerous in the second as she stepped into a lunging right hand, but back came Mayer with a right hook to the face while walking her opponent down in the corner.

Mayer was still seeking to find her range in the third, a short right leaving her open to a sharp Cameron counter, to which the American replied with a two-shot combination. Still, though, Cameron appeared content with a back-foot game-plan, leaning well on her timing and reaction to trouble Mayer.

As the distance began to close both began to let their hands go on the inside, Cameron clipping Mayer with a short right hook and Mayer digging into the body during a gritty exchange up-close.

Mayer then found some joy with a thumping right hand to the face of Cameron in the fifth before biting down on her gumshield as the rivals went toe-to-toe with another brutal trade of body shots on the inside.

A relentless pace showed no let-up as both unloaded body shots, before Cameron became the front-foot aggressor in the seventh behind a firm jab and follow-up right hand over the top. By the end of the seventh Cameron was stalking Mayer around the ring, the American unable to tailor the fight to her strengths.

By round nine swelling was evident on the face of both, Mayer wearing a cut to the eye and blood seemingly trickling from that of Cameron such had become a battle of attrition.

The two did notably embrace prior to their latest verbal altercation, no doubt in respect to a toiling contest between two of the sport's elite. Few would begrudge a rematch.

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Briton punches himself out and is stopped in round nine
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic shatters Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appears to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight world-title contest in London.
articles.body:
Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.

Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.

Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.

Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar.

"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind," Hrgovic said.

"From the first round, I saw his gassing out. He started fast. I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came I needed to push. That is what I did."

With the vacant IBF title on the line, victory would have made Itauma the second-youngest world champion in the division's history.

Instead, his inexperience began to show as his Croatian opponent - an Olympic bronze medallist whose only previous professional defeat came against Daniel Dubois - survived everything Itauma threw at him before completing a remarkable turnaround.

Wardley-Dubois rematch set for 17 October in London

Relive Hrgovic's dramatic stoppage win over Itauma to claim IBF heavyweight title - reaction

Cameron beats Mayer to become unified light-middleweight champion

Hrgovic's remarkable turnaround as Itauma shows inexperience

Hrgovic - wearing the red and white checks of his country - made his entrance first to a wall of boos, before the mood inside the O2 Arena flipped as Itauma emerged to a huge roar - taking his time and soaking up the reception.

The crowd had made its allegiances clear after a fiery build-up which included Itauma shoving Hrgovic, the Zagreb man slapping him back and plenty of verbal sparring.

Itauma came out with real intent, landing straight lefts from his southpaw stance. Hrgovic is known for his durability but struggled to keep pace with the Briton's speed early on.

Early in the second, a right hook knocked Hrgovic off-balance and his glove touched the canvas. Oasis star Noel Gallagher and boxing legend Prince Naseem Hamed were among those watching as the crowd gasped at almost every Itauma punch, whether it landed or not.

But by the end of the third, Itauma - who had boxed just 26 professional rounds before his first world-title fight - was already breathing heavily.

There had also been questions over his chin, simply because it had never really been tested. Hrgovic began landing the occasional heavy shot but Itauma took them well and fired straight back.

A fight in the crowd momentarily took attention away from the action in the fifth before an Itauma uppercut in the closing seconds brought the focus back to the ring.

Itauma continued to fire combinations but Hrgovic was barely budging. A huge right landed on the bell in the sixth and another followed in the seventh, yet the Croatian simply walked through them.

The Briton was well ahead but, rather than box his way towards victory, he continued to chase the knockout. A flurry in the eighth backed Hrgovic on to the ropes and had him in trouble, but Itauma was grimacing between exchanges and looking increasingly spent.

By now the danger was clear. Hrgovic came out with renewed purpose in the ninth and landed a thudding right which sent Itauma staggering backwards, almost through the ropes.

The youngster somehow stayed upright but his legs had gone. Hrgovic continued to press and when Itauma slumped into his corner, exhausted and barely able to defend himself, referee Howard Foster waved off the contest as the towel came in.

Hrgovic crashes the party - what next for Itauma?

Hrgovic admitted he had been "outboxed" but leaves London as Croatia's first heavyweight world champion, with Frank Sanchez waiting as the IBF mandatory challenger.

A unification fight could follow, with Daniel Dubois holding the WBO title and set to face Fabio Wardley again in October.

For Itauma, this was supposed to be a coronation.

Instead, he leaves the O2 Arena with questions over whether the step up came too soon.

He has time to rebuild and there will be a strong feeling that, with a little more experience, this night could have ended very differently.

Londoner Dubois was stopped by Joe Joyce as an unbeaten 23-year-old before going on to become a two-time world champion. Itauma has even more time on his side.

"He's an amazing fighter," Hrgovic said. "I am the present. He is definitely the future."

Promoter Frank Warren suggested Itauma was carrying a leg injury in the final round but backed him to return.

"Moses gave everything," he added. "He has to go back to the drawing board and he can come again."

The expectation around Itauma will not disappear entirely overnight but the aura of invincibility has gone.

articles.title: Filip Hrgovic stuns Moses Itauma with epic comeback as British heavyweight star loses unbeaten record
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic stopped Moses Itauma in the ninth round in one of the biggest shocks of the boxing year in London, with the 21-year-old paying the price for emptying his tank as Hrgovic became Croatia’s first-ever world heavyweight champion
articles.body:
Itauma, unbeaten coming into the fight and one of the sport's most talked about young talents, had started like a man intent on an early night and for six rounds barely lost a minute.

It looked like Itauma's bid to become Britain's second-youngest world champion was on course for success after a right hook to the temple rocked Hrgovic inside the opening minute, followed by a second-round left hook that forced the Croatian to steady himself with a glove on the canvas.

Itauma had won every round heading into the second half of the fight but that wasn't telling the full story.

Everything Itauma landed, including a fifth-round left uppercut detonated flush on the point of the chin, was absorbed by a man who had been in the deep waters before, and the effort of trying to move the immovable was draining the younger man with every round he banked.

The seventh round took Itauma beyond six rounds for the first time in his career, and the eighth broke him. Sensing his chance, he emptied the tank in a sustained assault, but Hrgovic stood firm and absorbed the punishment, leaving the young challenger almost completely spent.

Within a minute of the ninth Itauma was out on his feet, unable to hold himself steady as Hrgovic came forward, and his corner threw the towel with their man defenceless. He was attended by medical staff in his corner afterwards having given everything he had.

"Let me ask my young friend something," enquired Hrgovic. "Is a chin important? Chin is important.

"He's an amazing fighter – I want to thank him. To give me a chance to become a new superstar in the heavyweight division. I am the present. He is definitely the future.

"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind.

"From the first round, I saw him gassing out. He started fast, I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came, I needed to push. That is what I did."

For Hrgovic, it was the defining win of a long career, as his toughness and experience in boxing's hardest rooms were rewarded on a night when almost every scoring shot went against him. The victory also reshapes the heavyweight title picture, with the IBF belt now in Croatian hands.

For Itauma, a first professional defeat arrives as a brutal education rather than a humiliation, beaten not by a bigger puncher but by the questions of pace, patience and endurance that his early blowouts had never asked.

articles.title: Chantelle Cameron calls on WBC to implement three minute rounds for impending Mikaela Mayer title fight rematch
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron has called for a three-minute-round rematch against Mikaela Mayer after edging a tight contest 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 on the judges’ scorecards; Cameron’s coach says the Brit could vacate her WBC belt if three-minute rounds are not permitted for the rematch
articles.body:
The Brit edged a tight-knit contest 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 on the judges' scorecards after a thrilling contest, further glossing a stellar resume that already honours her as the only woman to ever defeat the great Katie Taylor in her professional career.

Cameron's rivalry with Mayer ignited after a a physical altercation and fierce war of words at their weigh-in resulted in them having to be split by security - and the new unified world champion is keen to see that that rivalry continues in another contest between the two:

"She wanted the weight, she wanted the twos [two-minute rounds], she wanted to have her name first, which is actually fine because we're not going to get into that," said Cameron in her post-fight press conference.

"If we want the rematch we have to do three-minute rounds. I'll speak to my team, I would like to do three-minute rounds, if it means vacating the WBC belt again I don't mind doing that."

Cameron, the only woman to beat Katie Taylor in the Irish great's professional career, put Saturday night's result to the top of her resume but downplayed suggestions she is the greatest female boxer of all time.

"I'll say it's my best win, I really enjoyed it tonight," she said. "I still think Claressa Shields is the best, I won't be deluded, Mikaela would, but Claressa is still No 1."

Tensions had boiled over on the eve of their fight as Cameron and Mayer clashed during a fiery weigh-in, an altercation the eventual victor believes worked in her favour come fight night.

"I think it she messed up, I think maybe it was too nicey nicey and friendly," said Cameron. "I did genuinely respect her. I was a fan of her. But the way she's coming on, I just think she's made a bit of a fool of herself.

"I knew that. I was looking at her before the bell rang and thought, I'm gonna smash your head in. And I think it worked.

"I was feeling the energy she didn't want to be in there, I could feel it."

The pair would later clash again following the final bell as Mayer disputed the decision, Cameron insisting any rematch would need to take place on her terms.

"I just wanted to play with [Mayer]," Cameron told Sky Sports after the fight. "If you're going to say you'll stop me, beat me easily... talk is so cheap, and I showed that tonight [Saturday]. Don't talk too much game - you've got to back it

"I want to do this again. It's up to Mikaela, but I want to do three-minute rounds.

"I'll speak to my team and see if Mikaela wants it, but - [to Mayer] - didn't you say you were going to beat me so bad that I wasn't going to want a rematch?"

The British boxer continued to goad her opponent, adding: "You were talking so much nonsense I actually fell asleep for a second!

"Go back to the gym, work on your power, work on your fitness, work on your speed, work on your boxing - make some improvements, because your team aren't doing a great job are they!

Mayer disputes result and pushes for rematch in USA

Mayer disputed the judges' decision after her defeat, claiming she "outboxed" Cameron on her own turf:

"I did beat you Chantelle. You are lucky in your little back yard.

"You can have your re-match. Three-minute rounds. If you want to vacate your WBC belt you can do that. It's your prerogative now. I'll just kick your ass even harder.

"But it won't be here. It won't be in the UK. If you want to come to the US you can.

"I outboxed you. I'll go back and rewatch it and give an honest evaluation, but I just beat you.

"If the public says I'm wrong you can have that... my initial feeling is I outboxed her."

Three-minute rounds could lead to WBC belt vacation, says Moore

Cameron's coach, Jamie Moore, says there is a possibility that Cameron could vacate the WBC title if they don't allow her to stage a three-minute round title defence against Mayer.

"I think in general, Chantelle is much better over three minutes.

"There's an issue with the WBC, and Chantelle is going to speak to her team to see if she might vacate the belt.

"Chantelle is adamant that - for female boxing moving forward - to be on the same level as men's boxing, it's got to be three-minute rounds."

articles.summary: Sete dos 17 pontos classificados como impróprios na região ficam em Santos. Boletim da Cetesb é válido até a próxima atualização, prevista para quinta-feira (3).
articles.body:
Praia em Santos (SP) — Foto: Matheus Müller/g1

Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, não tem praias próprias para banho nesta semana, segundo o boletim mais recente da Companhia Ambiental do Estado de São Paulo (Cetesb). Os sete pontos monitorados na cidade estão impróprios e representam sete dos 17 locais com restrição na Baixada Santista. A próxima atualização está prevista para quinta-feira (3).

O levantamento também mostra a situação das praias de São Vicente, Praia Grande, Guarujá, Mongaguá, Bertioga, Itanhaém e Peruíbe. Nessas cidades, pelo menos metade dos pontos analisados está própria para banho ( veja a tabela abaixo ).

A classificação da Cetesb é baseada na análise da quantidade de bactérias indicadoras de contaminação fecal encontrada na água. Para isso, são consideradas amostras coletadas durante cinco semanas consecutivas.

Praias impróprias para banho na Baixada Santista

Nas praias de água salgada, a Cetesb analisa a presença de enterococos. O ponto é considerado impróprio quando duas das cinco amostras passam de 100 UFC por 100 ml de água ou quando a coleta mais recente ultrapassa 400 UFC por 100 ml.

Os locais impróprios recebem bandeira vermelha, enquanto aqueles considerados próprios para banho são sinalizados com bandeira verde.

A Cetesb recomenda evitar o banho de mar nos pontos classificados como impróprios. Segundo a companhia, o contato com água contaminada pode aumentar o risco de infecções e outras doenças. A orientação também é:

⚠️Tomar banho de mar nas primeiras 24 horas após chuvas intensas; ⚠️Banhar-se em canais, córregos ou rios que afluem às praias; ⚠️Engolir água do mar; ⚠️Levar animais de estimação à praia.

Segundo a Cetesb, a doença mais comum associada ao contato com água contaminada é a gastroenterite, que pode provocar enjoo, vômitos, dor de estômago, diarreia, dor de cabeça e febre.

Também podem ocorrer infecções nos olhos, ouvidos, nariz e garganta. A companhia aponta ainda risco de doenças como hepatite A, cólera e febre tifoide.

articles.title: 'What in the hell??': Filip Hrgovic's unreal win over Moses Itauma leaves boxing world dumbfounded
articles.summary: After losing nearly every second of every round, Hrgovic mounted one of boxing's most improbable comebacks to stop an exhausted Itauma via ninth-round TKO.
articles.body:
For nearly eight rounds, it looked like a foregone conclusion that Moses Itauma was going to defeat Filip Hrgovic and capture the IBF heavyweight world title Saturday inside London's O2 Arena. Doing so would've made Itauma — a 21-year-old prodigy long hailed as a future of boxing's blue-ribbon division — the youngest heavyweight world champion since Mike Tyson knocked out Trevor Berbick in 1986 .

But then disaster struck. And now Hrgovic is first Croatia's first heavyweight champion — and the victor of one of the most surreal scenes in recent boxing history .

After losing nearly every second of every round, Hrgovic (21-1, 16 KOs) mounted an improbable comeback to stop an exhausted Itauma (14-1, 12 KOs) via ninth-round TKO. Ironically, it was Hrgovic's pre-fight emphasis on the value of a strong chin that proved to be most prophetic, as Hrgovic survived an outrageous onslaught of offense from the young phenom yet continued to push forward and stay in the fight.

Itauma had never made it out of the sixth round as a professional prior to Saturday night, and that inexperience reared its head at the worst of times, as the Briton barely appeared to have the energy to stand by the final round and was ultimately transported out of the arena on a stretcher after his team opted to throw in the towel.

Given that many assumed Itauma's coronation as heavyweight's new standard-bearer was an inevitability, it shouldn't come as a surprise that Saturday's result sent shockwaves throughout the boxing landscape. Check out how Shakur Stevenson, Jake Paul and more reacted to Hrgovic's career-changing performance below.

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: 'Moses Itauma will be world champion' - Stevenson, Bellew, Eubank Jr reaction
articles.summary: Shakur Stevenson and Tony Bellew believe Moses Itauma still has what it takes to become a world champion after losing to Filip Hrgovic for the IBF heavyweight title.
articles.body:
Shakur Stevenson and Tony Bellew believe Moses Itauma showed enough in defeat by Filip Hrgovic to suggest he will become a heavyweight world champion.

Itauma made a fast start at London's O2 Arena and controlled large parts of the contest for the vacant IBF title, but eventually ran out of steam and was stopped by Hrgovic in round nine.

The Briton's speed and power caught the eye early in the bout but once he broke new ground - going beyond the sixth round for the first time in his career - the wheels began to come off.

Hrgovic was outpunched in every round until the decisive ninth when he seized his moment to become Croatia's first heavyweight world champion.

BBC Radio 5 Live's coverage of the night ended with Richie Woodhall, Ronald McIntosh and Steve Bunce offering up one word each to describe the night.

"Incredible," former super-middleweight world champion Woodhall said.

"Unbelievable," added commentator McIntosh, while Bunce signed off with "unforgettable".

Relive Hrgovic's dramatic stoppage win over Itauma to claim IBF heavyweight title

Itauma punches himself out against Hrgovic in world-title fight

Many expected Itauma, who stepped into the ring with a perfect record of 14 wins as a professional, to be coronated as the next British heavyweight star - although Hrgovic was rightly touted as his biggest test to date.

Aged 21, Itauma was seeking to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion of all-time and Britain's second-youngest world champion.

But lack of experience against a seasoned Hrgovic proved Itauma's undoing.

Hype around Itauma has been building since winning his pro debut in just 23 seconds in January 2023.

A string of highlight knockouts - winning 12 of his previous 14 bouts inside six rounds - had propelled the Chatham fighter to world-title level in quick fashion.

Despite coming up short against 34-year-old Hrgovic, he is still being tipped to reach the pinnacle of boxing's glamour division.

"Unbelievable talent and skills," four-weight world champion Stevenson wrote on X.

"He's young and will be a champion one day if he learns from that. He throws every punch at 100mph and that can be a gift and a curse, Especially in the heavyweights division!"

Fellow Briton Tony Bellew, who was a cruiserweight world champion but ended his career at heavyweight, was also keen to focus on the positives.

"Moses Itauma will be world champion! He will learn so much from tonight," Bellew posted on X.

"The biggest thing I'll take from tonight is just how brave and tough Moses was, we knew Filip was super tough. Tonight we learned Moses is also tough, once he learns to pace a 12-round bout, he's gonna rule for a while! Filip Hrgovic's chin needs to studied."

Itauma told BBC Sport in the weeks before his heavyweight title fight that he had never even sparred 12 rounds, and it showed as he grew fatigued with each round that passed.

Trainer Ben Davison almost threw in the towel early in the ninth round as Itauma staggered around the ring, but he had second thoughts.

It was only moments later that the towel did come in as referee Howard Foster had stepped in to wave off the contest with Itauma unable to stand without the ropes to aid him.

Chris Eubank Jr wrote on X: "Not sure what happened tonight. Moses was fighting well and then gassed out it seems… at his young age this should simply not be happening. Time to rethink his training camp moving forward I think."

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: British heavyweight given a hard lesson on the realities of world-level boxing
articles.summary: British heavyweight Moses Itauma was taught a harsh lesson at world level - what can he learn from defeat and where does the 21-year-old go next?
articles.body:
Moses Itauma was still a schoolboy when he would turn up at boxing gyms in his uniform and give seasoned professionals a hiding.

On Saturday night at the O2 Arena, the 21-year-old was finally given an education, as the Briton ran out of gas and the granite experience of Filip Hrgovic carried the Croatian to the vacant IBF heavyweight title.

The referee waved off the fight as Itauma's corner threw in the towel in the ninth round. But for long spells, Itauma was the quicker, sharper and more assured fighter, repeatedly finding Hrgovic with the left hand and showing exactly why so many inside boxing believe he has the tools to reach the very top.

Yet what made the contest so compelling was the growing sense that, even while Itauma was winning rounds, he was drifting closer to defeat.

'Unbelievable' - Stephenson, Bellew & others react to Hrgovic's stoppage of Itauma

Wardley-Dubois rematch set for 17 October in London

His mouth opened in search of air and the spring disappeared from his legs. Hrgovic, hardened by the kind of difficult nights Itauma had never experienced, simply stayed there and waited for the younger man's body to betray him.

The sight afterwards was a sobering one as Itauma - who suffered a first defeat in his 15th pro fight - left the arena on a stretcher, before being taken to hospital.

"It's precautionary that he's gone to the hospital. That's what we always do to make sure because the most important thing is the boxer's health," promoter Frank Warren said.

"He's done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high paced, fast fight for both the guys."

The remarkable night should not be remembered as the moment Itauma was exposed as incapable of operating at world level - his boxing showed the opposite.

What it exposed was the difference between possessing world-level talent and having the conditioning, experience and ring craft required to manage a 12-round world-title fight.

It would be too simplistic - and unfair - to say Hrgovic won the fight purely through mind games, but the 34-year-old had succeeded in making the build-up uncomfortable.

Hrgovic spent fight week repeatedly attacking Itauma's age, dismissing him as "just a kid". As the week wore on, Itauma looked increasingly irritated and eventually lost his composure at the weigh-in, shoving Hrgovic before the Croatian responded with a slap.

Itauma prides himself on being unusually cerebral for a heavyweight. He reads psychology and self-help books, talks openly about sharpening his mind and appears to spend far more time analysing himself than most 21-year-olds.

But there is always a danger that deep thinking becomes overthinking, something Anthony Joshua has been accused of repeatedly during the latter stages of his career.

Whether the pre-fight barbs played any part or not, Itauma's gameplan once the bell rang was clear; he wanted to end the night early.

"Someone said to me he doesn't feel like he'd win a world title unless he knocks him out. I didn't like that," promoter Frank Warren said afterwards.

That mindset was understandable because it had served Itauma extraordinarily well until now. But perhaps Hrgovic had been underestimated by almost everybody - Itauma, the media, pundits, former fighters and bookmakers who installed the Briton as a heavy favourite.

Hrgovic is an Olympic bronze medallist who went 12 hard rounds with the giant Zhilei Zhang, while against Daniel Dubois - the only defeat on his record - he was leading on two of the three scorecards before the fight was stopped because of cuts.

'El Animal' knew what it felt like to be hurt, to become tired and to remain in a fight when things were going badly. Itauma did not.

The eighth round summed up both Itauma's extraordinary talent and his lack of experience. He threw more punches than in any other round of the fight, pouring what remained of his energy into trying to remove a man who had already demonstrated that he was exceptionally difficult to remove.

"He was throwing too much. He was fighting like an amateur," Hrgovic said afterwards. "I knew I needed to endure it. I need to stay there. He will get tired and I'll get him in the later rounds."

There are questions about the Chatham fighter's preparation, too. Itauma - who had never gone beyond six rounds professionally - admitted before the fight that he had never even sparred 12 rounds.

His conditioning was clearly not where it needed to be for a championship fight and responsibility for that cannot rest solely with the fighter - it also falls on the experienced team entrusted with preparing him.

Educated, not exposed - will Itauma learn his lesson?

Itauma showed that many of the qualities which looked spectacular against lesser opposition still worked against a genuine world-level heavyweight.

He proved he can take a punch - there was no single blow that suddenly revealed a fragile chin. His hand speed troubled Hrgovic and he made the Zagreb fighter look slow.

So with those positives in mind, where does he go from here?

"Don't give up. Don't lose confidence. Get a few easy fights, easy wins. Build again and learn off these mistakes. You can't box like an amateur. It's a 12-round fight, you need to pace yourself," was Hrgovic's advice.

Warren remains convinced that Itauma is one of the most exceptional talents he has encountered, pointing towards two-time world champion Dubois as a prime example of a heavyweight who rebuilt successfully after painful setbacks.

But British boxing has seen the other side of that story too, of course - where fighters like David Price were once regarded as the country's next great heavyweight hope before successive defeats damaged an aura they never fully recovered.

Audiences will now scrutinise Itauma's every move, his breathing and how he paces a fight. That vulnerability may actually make him a more compelling fighter to follow.

The aura of untouchable perfection is gone. The schoolboy has been taught a lesson and now we will find out what he learns from it.

articles.title: Usman Nurmagomedov Has Statement on UFC Shanghai Incident
articles.summary: Usman Nurmagomedov issued a statement following the incident at UFC Shanghai after his brother was knocked out in the main event.After Umar Nurmagomedov was...
articles.body:
Usman Nurmagomedov issued a statement following the incident at UFC Shanghai after his brother was knocked out in the main event.

After Umar Nurmagomedov was shockingly knocked out by Song Yadong in the UFC Shanghai headliner, Usman Nurmagomedov — who was in his brother's corner — immediately jumped the fence and got into the Octagon because he wanted to tend to his fallen brother.

It just so happens that Song was celebrating his win and nearly ran into Usman Nurmagomedov — who should not have been in the Octagon at that point — which nearly led to disaster, as Usman Nurmagomedov pushed him away and then wound up throwing a backwards elbow at him, though he ultimately held up from doing so.

The Russian was widely criticized online for the incident, one that could have ended far worse had the blow connected on Song's chin.

Now, he is speaking out and sharing his side of the story.

Usman Nurmagomedov Issues Statement on UFC Shanghai Incident

Taking to his social media, the PFL lightweight champion issued a statement on the UFC Shanghai incident, suggesting that he would have hit Song had he wanted to, and that he feels like the criticism is only coming from jealous people.

"Only what is ordained for us will befall us. In any situation—Alhamdulillah. People make such a huge tragedy out of this; they really ought to calm down. There are far worse things; you don't need to think long—just look at what is happening in the world. And as for the claim that I supposedly wanted to hit his opponent… If I had wanted to, I would have hit him. You spiteful, petty, and envious people—your problem is that you have never known, nor will you ever know, family love and understanding. If you don't know what a brother means to a brother, then it is not me you should pity, but yourselves," Nurmagomedov wrote on his Instagram.

The biggest issue for Usman Nurmagomedov is that he jumped the Octagon and got into the cage before the cornermen were supposed to, which could land him in hot water with the UFC , which sanctioned this event in China.

Had this fight taken place in Las Vegas, he would most likely be in serious trouble and could potentially lose his corner's license for jumping into the Octagon, never mind running into Song.

Yes, it is never easy seeing a family member get hurt and knocked out. But the Nurmagomedov brothers are not the only pair of siblings who have seen their family members get hurt and lose in the UFC, yet this is the only time something like this has happened in recent memory.

Will this affect Usman Nurmagomedov potentially signing with the UFC as a free agent? Likely not, because he is a great talent and the UFC would love to have him in their lightweight division.

But the fact that he is doubling down on what happened and not taking the high road and apologizing to Song is not a great look.

articles.title: Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic secured one of the biggest shocks in boxing this year after stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2; Hrgovic becomes Croatia's first-ever world heavyweight champion
articles.body:
Hrgovic, 34, became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion at The O2 on Saturday night to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title.

Itauma, 21, who was unbeaten coming into the bout, was dominant in the first six rounds after landing a string of accurate blows.

But he became visibly exhausted as the fight progressed and he failed to find a way past Hrgovic's durable chin, with the seventh round being the first time in his career he had been past six rounds.

The Croatian then pounced in the ninth round, which forced the Brit's corner to throw in the towel.

Following his win, Hrgovic hailed Itauma as the most talented fighter in the heavyweight division but said his boxing reminded him of the amateur ranks.

Hrgovic said: "Let me be honest, he's amazing. I didn't know it was going to be so hard, I thought I was going to handle him easier.

"I was losing all the rounds. The kid is amazing, he was so fast, you don't see his punches coming.

"He doesn't hit so hard but he's fast. But since the first (round) I saw he was gassing out, he was boxing still like an amateur.

"He's inexperienced, I saw he was gassing out and I knew my only chance was to stay there to make him tired, to keep coming and to maybe stop him later on. That's what I did.

"I came to London, his hometown, against the most talented guy in the division and I beat all the odds.

"I want to be considered the best heavyweight in the world, and this is my time. I am the best. I am the present and he is the future.

"I want to fight for unification against Dubois or Agit Kabayel. I want to go for unification, that's what I want."

Itauma came into the fight lauded as one of the sport's brightest young talents after some early knockout wins.

But he will have to work on pacing himself for fights that go beyond the halfway point against durable opponents like Hrgovic.

Itauma was carried from the ring on a stretcher and taken to hospital following the stoppage as a precautionary measure.

Promoter Frank Warren said: "That's what we always do to make sure because the most important thing is the boxer's health.

"He's there and he's in the best place. We'll see what happens when I've got a report. We'll obviously let everybody know.

"He's done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high-paced, fast fight for both the guys. It was just edge of your seat stuff all the way through."

Itauma came into the fight hoping to be crowned Britain's youngest ever heavyweight world champion, but Warren said it was now unclear what his next move would be.

Warren added: "I don't know what he's going to say. I'm sure he's a fighting man. He showed that right to the end. At the end, that's the type of fight it was - they were standing there just letting bombs go.

"I don't even know how he feels mentally. Mentally, he's going to be completely down. We're going to have to talk to him and lift him and see what he's like.

"It's going to take some time. He's going to have a nice break. It's not even the time to talk about it with him at the moment.

"It's something we're probably doing in two weeks or even a month's time, see where we go with it."

Hrgovic must now take on the IBF's mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez.

articles.title: Filip Hrgovic defeats Moses Itauma in London to become heavyweight boxing champion
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic absorbed blow after blow before stopping Moses Itauma in the ninth round to hand the 21-year-old British boxer his first loss and take the vacant IBF heavyweight world title on Saturday.
articles.body: LONDON — Filip Hrgovic absorbed blow after blow before stopping Moses Itauma in the ninth round to hand the 21-year-old British boxer his first loss and take the vacant IBF heavyweight world title on Saturday. Itauma’s corner threw in the towel as he was being pummelled against the ropes, making the 34-year-old Hrgovic the first Croatian heavyweight champion. Itauma had never needed to go past the sixth round in his first 14 professional bouts and tired visibly after taking command of the early rounds, with Hrgovic absorbing a barrage of hits even after being knocked down in the second round. The rivals traded blows in the eighth and ninth before the granite chin of Hrgovic won out. “I was losing every round. I was outboxed. And I don’t know from where I got energy,” Hrgovic said. “Look, chin is important.” Hrgovic improved to 22-1 and halted the rapid rise of Itauma, who was trying to become the youngest heavyweight champion since a 20-year-old Mike Tyson stopped Trevor Berbick in 1986. Itauma couldn’t stand after the bout ended and was treated by medical personnel before being helped out of the ring. “He’s an amazing fighter,” Hrgovic said. “I’m the present. And he’s definitely the future. ... He’s the best I’ve been in the ring with. But he needs more experience. He gassed out.” Unification bout next? Promoter Frank Warren said after the bout that Hrgovic is set to next fight Cuban Frank Sanchez, but the Croatian himself said he instead wants to take on WBO champion Daniel Dubois and then WBC title holder Agit Kabayel — both of whom were ringside at the O2 Arena. “I want unification. Frank Sanchez will wait,” Hrgovic said. Hrgovic’s only loss came to Dubois in 2024. Hrgovic was bleeding from deep cuts above his eyes that time when the ringside doctor recommended the fight be stopped.

articles.title: Moses Itauma unlikely to receive Filip Hrgovic rematch after shock heavyweight stoppage defeat
articles.summary: Moses Itauma suffered a surprise ninth-round stoppage defeat to Filip Hrgovic at The O2 in London; 21-year-old British contender faces being unable to secure an immediate rematch
articles.body:
The 21-year-old British contender inflicted a second round knockdown on Hrgovic, but then tired dramatically before being stopped in the ninth round at The O2 in London on Saturday night.

Itauma could now be forced to wait for another world title fight as no 1 contender Frank Sanchez is mandatory challenger for the IBF title after initially agreeing a deal to allow Itauma vs Hrgovic to go ahead first.

Hrgovic is also obliged to face Sanchez before he can pursue a unification bout against fellow champions such as Agit Kabayel, Daniel Dubois and Murat Gassiev.

Sanchez's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports: "Per the IBF, no intervening bout, including unification bouts, are permitted prior to the satisfaction of Frank Sanchez's mandatory.

"That said, Queensberry is going to be our partner on Frank's next bout, presumably versus Hrgovic, and we will discuss that in the coming days with Frank and George Warren.

"For eight rounds Moses was brilliant. He will be back better, much like Daniel Dubois after his first loss.

"I spoke to Frank Sanchez and [his trainer] Eddy Reynoso immediately following the bout. Both are ready and excited for Hrgovic next.

"In the meantime, congratulations to my friends [manager] Keith Connolly and Filip Hrgovic. Keep the title warm, because Frank Sanchez is coming."
