articles.title: Watch Britt Baker Return at AEW All In to Cost Maya World TBS Title vs. Persephone in Viral Video
articles.summary: Sunday's TBS Championship match between Maya World and Persephone during The Buy In pre-show of AEW's All In pay-per-view was interrupted by a highly anticipated return.
articles.body:
Sunday's TBS Championship match between Maya World and Persephone during The Buy In pre-show of AEW's All In pay-per-view was interrupted by a highly anticipated return.

During the closing moments of the match, a masked figure attacked World, allowing Persephone to pick up the win and claim the TBA title. After the match, the attacker took off her mask and was revealed to be former AEW Women's World Champion Britt Baker:

Baker hasn't been seen in AEW since her last match in November 2024. During the All In media call this past week, AEW CEO Tony Khan teased her potential return at the flagship PPV.

"Britt Baker is somebody who is an AEW original and has competed at All In London previously," Khan said at the time . "I know fans are always excited about Britt and asking about Britt. The last time we were in Wembley Stadium, Britt was on the show. I would say, as with all the questions about people returning or debuting, anytime we're getting asked about somebody coming back to AEW TV or debuting, I've always said, Stay tuned.' In this case, I would say that makes sense as well."

However, fans had the wind taken out of their sails on Friday when a report from Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News) revealed, "This should not be a surprise, but Britt Baker is not in London." It's now clear that AEW was able to keep her return under wraps for a massive surprise.

After winning the TBS title to go along with her CMLL Women's Championship, Persephone made her alliance with Baker official and targeted Thunder Rosa in a backstage interview:

Baker's return adds even more intrigue to the AEW women's division, which is already filled with impressive talent and exciting storylines.

articles.title: AEW All In 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From Wembley Stadium
articles.summary: AEW returned to Wembley Stadium Sunday for its All In pay-per-view extravaganza, headlined by London's native son, Will Ospreay, challenging Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
AEW returned to Wembley Stadium Sunday for its All In pay-per-view extravaganza, headlined by London's native son, Will Ospreay, challenging Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.

Did the Aerial Assassin pay off his arduous journey, including neck surgery, and win the title in front of his family and friends, or did Omega once again prove to be the hurdle he cannot overcome?

Find out the answer to that and more in this recap, including grades and analysis for each of the card's bouts.

AEW World Championship Match: Kenny Omega (c) vs. Will Ospreay

AEW World Women's Championship Match: Willow Nightingale (c) vs. Mercedes Mone

AEW World Tag Team Championship Match: Cope and Christian Cage (c) vs. The Young Bucks

AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship Match: The Brawling Birds vs. Divine Dominion (c)

AEW International Championship Match: Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kyle Fletcher (c) vs. Kazuchika Okada

Falls Count Anywhere Match for the TNT Championship: Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight (c)

Continental Challenge Cup Final for the Continental Championship: Nigel McGuinnes vs. Jon Moxley (c)

Casino Gauntlet Match: Andrade El Idolo vs. MJF vs. Tommaso Ciampa vs. More to be announced

Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championship: Hangman Page and Brodido (c) vs. The Death Riders vs. The Demand vs. The Bang Bang Gang vs. The Conglomeration vs. The Dogs

TBS Championship Match: Maya World (c) vs. Persephone

8-Man Tag Team Match: The Hurt Business, Big Boom AJ, and QT Marshall vs. Shane Taylor Promotions

Harley Cameron and Kris Statlander vs. Skye Blue and Julia Hart

The Rascalz and Lio Rush defeated Action Andretti, Hook, Anthony Bowens, and Katsuyori Shibata

A fun, energetic match that highlighted both teams, especially the popular Rush, this was a great tone-setter as fans continued to arrive at the stadium. The babyfaces went over, too, with the look on Andretti's face after the match suggesting that he and Rush are headed toward a showdown over his Ring of Honor Television Championship.

Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron defeated Skye Blue and Julia Hart

This was a short, formulaic match featuring Cameron fighting from underneath before making the tag that decided the outcome. Statlander proved the difference as she drove Hart down with Saturday Night Fever for the win. Statlander and Cameron are very popular, but the Triangle of Madness is a legitimate team that would have benefited from winning here.

The Hurt Business and Doom and Boom defeated Shane Taylor Promotions

A high-energy bout down the stretch showcased all eight competitors and had the fans more invested than they were earlier in the bout. The babyfaces predictably went over, with Lashley putting Charlie Bravo down with the Dominator for the win. There was an interesting booking decision late, with Trish Adora and Christyan XO distracting Bryce Remsburg, which allowed Big Justice to interfere and join his dad for a double spear spot. They remained on the apron when it was clearly hurting their charges, which made little sense.

TBS Championship Match: Persephone defeated Maya World to win the title

A good, competitive match, but it never had the audience completely invested as one would hope given the recent stature of both women on AEW TV. This was a solid showing by World, but her opponent stood out, thanks to her in-ring work and the ability to tell the match's story through facial expressions and body language.

Late in the match, a masked and hooded individual shoved the It Girl from the top rope, allowing Persephone to win the match and the title. After the match, Dr. Britt Baker revealed herself to be under the mask in the night's first big moment, of which there are expected to be several.

Trios Roulette Royale for the AEW World Trios Championship

Order of entry: Bang Bang Gang, The Dogs, The Demand, The Conglomeration, The Death Riders, Hangman Page and Brodido, Swerve Strickland and The New Level

Austin Creed and Kofi took things to a New Level Sunday in London, arriving in AEW as the partners of Swerve Strickland in the Trios Roulette Royale to a thunderous ovation.

Their arrival was only one highlight of a match that featured several stories and rivalries intertwined throughout, including that of the Bang Bang Gang and The Dogs, as well as Strickland and Page. The elimination of the latter by Ricochet guaranteed new champions.

Strickland and New Level would pay off their debut outing by eliminating the competition and claiming the titles, capping off an excellent match that started slowly, with too many wrestlers in the ring at once, but improved with every passing minute, culminating in a crowd-pleasing moment and a career-defining one for Creed and Kofi.

AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship Match: Brawling Birds vs. Divine Dominion

Last Time in Action: Divine Dominion and Persephone defeated Maya World and The Brawling Birds (Dynamite, August 26)

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross faced the toughest test of their reign as champions on Sunday, battling England's own Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor in the main show's opening contest.

The heels isolated Hayter early, wearing her down in their corner of the ring. A pair of clotheslines allowed the former world champion to fend off the champions and make the tag to Windsor, who spurred the babyface comeback.

As the action rolled on, each team took turns unloading their arsenals, neither able to keep the other down. The heels teed off on Hayter, driving her to the mat with a double chokeslam, but Windsor broke up the pin.

The challengers survived the punishing offense of their dominant opponents and finished Kross off with Two Birds, One Stone for the win and the titles.

This was a strong match with some great tag team work from both teams and a finish that saw the right team take the titles.

Hayter and Windsor beat the seemingly unbeatable, but who of the other teams in the division stand a realistic shot at dethroning them?

The Brawling Birds defeated Divine Dominion to win the titles

Kross and Bayne are a success story as a team thrown together that managed to develop into a great tandem, with strong chemistry, who carried the women's tag division on their backs for five months.

Hayter and Windsor getting the home country win was a great moment for them and pays off what has been a string of great performances. They could be the anchor piece for the division moving forward.

Continental Cup Final for the AEW Continental Championship: Nigel McGuinness vs. Jon Moxley

Last Time in Action: Jon Moxley defeated Claudio Castagnoli (Dynamite, August 26); Nigel McGuinness defeated Kyle O'Reilly (Dynamite, August 26)

The AEW Continental Championship and victory in this year's Continental Challenge Cup tournament were on the line as London's own Nigel McGuinness battled Jon Moxley in the second match of the main card.

Moxley targeted his opponent's lower leg and ankle while McGuinness worked over his opponent's left arm. The challenger flattened the champion with a Tower of London, rocked his opponent with a tandem of lariats, then escaped the bulldog choke and applied the London Dungeon submission hold.

None of it was enough to keep the Death Rider down or force a tapout.

Instead, Moxley absorbed everything thrown at him by the former Ring of Honor world champion and trapped him in an ankle lock. McGuinness showed tremendous grit and toughness as he fought through the pain to come within an inch of the ropes, only for the suffering to be too great to overcome. He tapped out, awarding the match and the Continental Cup to Moxley.

The best match of the night to this point, it featured some excellent grappling from McGuinness, and Moxley looked competent wrestling that style of match. He may not be the great worker that some believe him to be, but outwrestling McGuinness in Wembley is an enormous feat. Hanging with the measuring stick for toughness in AEW is a testament to the runner-up, too.

Moxley defeated McGuinness to retain the title

Moxley survived a Tower of London before trading LeBelle Locks with his opponent, all while Bryan Danielson called the action on commentary, in a nice ode to the former world champion.

McGuinness countered a sunset flip, stacking Moxley high on his shoulders in an homage to Bret Hart vs. British Bulldog from SummerSlam 1992, a match the challenger watched in the same Wembley Stadium as a child. A great callback.

AEW International Championship Match: Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada vs. Kyle Fletcher

Last Time in Action: Kyle Fletcher defeated Mike Bailey (Dynamite, August 5); Kazuchika Okada, Hechicero, and Kevin Knight lost to Corazon de Leon, Darby Allin, and Mistico (Dynamite, August 5); Konosuke Takeshita defeated The Beast Mortos (Collision, August 26)

"Protostar" Kyle Fletcher defended the AEW International Championship against "Rainmaker" Kazuchika Okada and Konosuke Takeshita in a Three-Way Dance.

The Don Callis Family further disintegrated when two miscommunications led to Okada and Fletcher taking each other out. The latter followed with a lariat of his own to The Rainmaker, resulting in Callis noting on commentary, "We're all sportsmen in the Don Callis Family."

Takeshita delivered a Powerdrive Knee to Fletcher, followed by Raging Fire, but Okada broke up the pin and landed the Rainmaker to his former partner-turned-enemy. Fletcher broke that pin up to save his title reign.

Moments later, Fletcher fired up, brought Takeshita from the top rope and appeared to be on his way to victory. Instead, Okada appeared and flattened his DCF stablemate with the Rainmaker to win the match and the title.

After the match, Fletcher awarded Okada the title, then reluctantly raised the victor's hand.

This a predictably great match. The talent involved nearly guaranteed as much. Fletcher continued to showcase the skills that have made him the brightest young star in AEW. Ditto, Takeshita.

The finish was interesting in that Okada distinctly chose to pin Fletcher, even though he easily could have pinned the other opponent. His actions after the match, demanding The Protostar raise his hand, make one think that Fletcher may be on his way out of the faction.

Okada defeated Fletcher and Takeshita to win the title

Fletcher hit the ring dressed as Donquixote Doflamingo from One Piece . Great pop culture reference and one that fit his pink color scheme.

Takeshita followed Okada up, then delivered a bridging German suplex to Fletcher, for a creative double-pin spot.

Okada is delightful as the grinning, disingenuous, braggadocios villain.

Casino Gauntlet Match to Determine the No. 1 Contender

Order of Entry: Andrade El Idolo, MJF, Nick Wayne, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, Tommaso Ciampa, Chris Jericho, Mark Davis, Komander, Mistico, Daniel Garcia , Jungle Jack Perry

Andrade El Idolo earned a future shot at the AEW World Championship by way of his win in the Casino Gauntlet Match Sunday in London.

He overcame an early battle with rival MJF, as well as the arrivals of former world champions and young stars with plenty to prove, to capture the title in an entertaining match. Still, it lacked the overall quality of other matches of its kind.

One thing the contest did do was play up the idea that if a fall was scored before all competitors could enter the ring, those wrestlers would miss out on an opportunity to compete for the top prize in the company.

That is exactly what happened, according to the commentary team, as El Idolo delivered MJF's Heat Seeker to Nick Wayne for the win and title shot.

Some will argue this could have been better served as a one-on-one match between Andrade and MJF and while they may have a point, this format allowed one to win without the other suffering an unnecessary loss. Even better? That singles match can take place at a later date, on a show where it will not be overshadowed by other main events.

The unannounced time intervals allowed for more unpredictability and creative convenience. It also felt cheap in that it adapted the rules to fit the stories AEW wanted to tell rather than the other way around.

This might have been the most inconsequential appearance by Jericho on an AEW pay-per-view ever.

The meteoric rise of El Idolo in this return to AEW has been refreshing for his fans, who did not have a lot to be excited about in the last handful of years.

articles.title: New Day's Kofi Kingston, Xavier Woods Win AEW Titles as New Level in Debut at All In After WWE Exit
articles.summary: After a 12-year run as a team in WWE, New Day's Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their AEW debut Sunday at All In as New Level under the names Kofi and Awesome Austin Creed.
articles.body:
After a 12-year run as a team in WWE, New Day's Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their AEW debut Sunday at All In as New Level under the names Kofi and Awesome Austin Creed.

Kofi and Creed emerged at Wembley Stadium in London as the surprise tag team partners for Swerve Strickland in the AEW Trios Roulette Royale.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Swerve, Kofi and Creed won the match to dethrone "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido as AEW World Trios Champions. Kofi and Creed are now the first AEW wrestlers to win a title in their first appearance in the company.

The professional wrestling world was left in a state of shock in May when Kingston and Woods left WWE after 20 and 16 years with the company, respectively.

It was later reported by Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News) that Kingston and Woods made the decision to leave WWE after being asked to take a pay cut.

When Kingston and Woods officially became free agents 90 days after their WWE release, they posted an animated video on X that seemed to indicate they had left WWE and were preparing to write their next chapter in pro wrestling:

For most of its existence, New Day was a three-man unit comprised of Kingston, Woods and Big E in WWE. In any iteration, New Day is the most-decorated tag team in WWE history with 12 tag team title reigns, including a record for the longest singular reign at 483 days.

When Big E suffered a serious neck injury in 2022 that rendered him unable to wrestle any longer, Kingston and Woods continued to use the New Day moniker as a duo.

Individually, the 45-year-old Kingston was a four-time intercontinental champion and three-time United States champion. He also won the WWE Championship at WrestleMania 35 in one of the most memorable moments in WrestleMania history.

Woods, 39, never held a singles title in WWE, but he did win the 2021 King of the Ring tournament.

With Kingston and Woods now in AEW, they figure to become a featured part of an already stacked tag team division that includes The Young Bucks, Cope and Cage, FTR, The Motor City Machine Guns and many others.

articles.title: Brawling Birds Beat Divine Dominion to Win AEW Women's Tag Titles at All In 2026 at Wembly
articles.summary: The Brawling Birds defeated Divine Dominion at All In 2026 on Sunday to win the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships at Wembley Stadium in London.
articles.body:
The Brawling Birds defeated Divine Dominion at All In 2026 on Sunday to win the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships at Wembley Stadium in London.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross entered All In as the longest-reigning AEW women's tag team champions in the brief history of the titles, as they had held them since March.

Divine Dominion beat the inaugural titleholders, Willow Nightingale and Harley Cameron, at the Revolution pay-per-view, and they were champions for over five months by the time All In rolled around.

After winning the championships, Bayne and Kross ran through many of the top women's tag teams AEW has to offer, including Kris Statlander and Hikaru Shida, Tay Melo and Anna Jay, and Julia Hart and Skye Blue.

Arguably the one notable team that Divine Dominion could not solve was The Brawling Birds, as Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor teamed with Willow to beat Bayne, Kross and Mercedes Moné in a six-woman tag team match on Dynamite earlier this month.

Following that bout, Hayter and Windsor against Bayne and Kross for the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships was made official for All In.

The Brawling Birds were a fitting choice to oppose Divine Dominion because of the added meaning that came along with All In being held in London.

Both Hayter and Windsor are from England, giving them a distinct home-field advantage over Bayne and Kross, who are from the United States and Australia, respectively.

While Bayne and Kross undoubtedly had the size and strength edge, Hayter and Windsor had the benefit of being able to draw inspiration from the large crowd that packed into Wembley.

With the London faithful cheering them on, The Brawling Birds ended Divine Dominion's lengthy title reign and became the third women's tag team champs in AEW history.

articles.title: Jon Moxley Beats Nigel McGuinness to Retain AEW Continental Title at All In 2026 at Wembley
articles.summary: Jon Moxley beat Nigel McGuinness in McGuinness' hometown of London at AEW All In on Sunday to retain the Continental Championship.
articles.body:
Jon Moxley beat Nigel McGuinness in McGuinness' hometown of London at AEW All In on Sunday to retain the Continental Championship.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Sunday's bout was the culmination of the Continental Challenge Cup, which saw 16 AEW stars compete for the opportunity to have a continental title match at All In.

Despite holding the Continental Championship since December, Mox was included in the tourney, meaning he would have to run the table in order to keep the title in his possession.

Moxley impressively made his way to the finals by beating Jack Perry in the first round and Jay White in the quarterfinals before getting the better of Death Riders stablemate Claudio Castagnoli in the semis.

At 50 years of age, McGuinness was the oldest participant in the tournament, but he was a sentimental favorite due to the possibility of him getting to have a big match in his home country of England at All In.

McGuinness quickly went from an underdog to a true title contender by beating Katsuyori Shibata in the first round, Hechicero in the quarterfinals and Kyle O'Reilly in the semifinals.

With that, McGuinness' ticket was punched to Wembley Stadium and his biggest match since returning to the squared circle two years ago.

McGuinness ended a 13-year absence from in-ring competition at All In 2024 by taking part in the Casino Gauntlet, and it was fitting that his match against Moxley happened at the same venue.

While McGuinness' return has been a great story in pro wrestling, a one-on-one match against arguably the most successful wrestler in AEW history at All In was an entirely different challenge than anything else he has faced the past two years.

Although McGuinness looked like he belonged on Sunday, Mox denied him what would have been the first title win of his AEW career.

articles.title: Okada Beats Fletcher, Takeshita to Win AEW International Title at All In 2026 at Wembley
articles.summary: Kazuchika Okada beat Kyle Fletcher and Konosuke Takeshita in a three-way match at AEW All In on Sunday to win the International Championship.
articles.body:
Kazuchika Okada beat Kyle Fletcher and Konosuke Takeshita in a three-way match at AEW All In on Sunday to win the International Championship.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Okada had the chance to pin Takeshita, but he chose to pin Fletcher, likely setting up a rivalry between the two Don Callis Family members.

After winning the International Championship for the first time last month, Fletcher was almost instantly met with a massive challenge for All In.

In Okada and Takeshita, Fletcher had to face the two wrestlers who held the international title immediately before him.

While a rematch with Takeshita was expected after Fletcher beat him for the International Championship at the Beach Break edition of Dynamite, Okada's inclusion was a bit of a curveball.

Don Callis, who manages both Fletcher and Okada, broke the news to Fletcher, theorizing that adding another member of The Don Callis Family to the match would give them a better chance of keeping the title in the stable.

Takeshita, who is a former member of The Don Callis Family, made his AEW return on the Aug. 19 episode of Dynamite after being away from the company for over a month in order to compete in New Japan Pro-Wrestling's G1 Climax tournament.

The Alpha interrupted a Don Callis Family meeting that saw Fletcher and Okada agree to work together at All In to ensure that Takeshita would not win back the international title.

Takeshita attacked Fletcher and left him laying due to the fact that Okada bailed rather than lending his stablemate a helping hand.

Because of that, there was plenty of tension between Fletcher and Okada entering All In, and no guarantee that they would be on the same page.

Even so, Okada rose to the occasion on the big stage and defeated both Fletcher and Takeshita to become a two-time international champion.

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer admits Chantelle Cameron's trash talk 'triggered' her as American expresses regret for post-fight antics
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer says she "acted in a way that I shouldn't have" after Saturday's defeat to Chantelle Cameron in Birmingham; the American has accepted the decision a day after claiming victory in the ring; a rematch clause is in the contract with Mayer open to three-minute rounds
articles.body:
The defeat was just the third of Mayer's professional career and cost her the unified belts she had brought to Birmingham, a breathless contest between two of the sport's pound-for-pound elite living up to its billing and strengthening Cameron's claim to a place among the greats of the women's game.

The pair had to be separated by security after a physical altercation at Friday's weigh-in and clashed again in the ring on Saturday night, with Mayer telling the new unified WBA, WBC and WBO champion "I did beat you" after the judges scored it 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 against her.

Speaking to Sky Sports News , Mayer said: "In the heat of the moment after the fight, I felt I had won, but I knew it was close, and I was prepared to go to the mic and give her her props and say I'm looking forward to the rematch.

"I'm not going to lie, I heard her on the mic talking trash and it triggered me. It brought something out of me and I feel like I acted in a way that I shouldn't have."

Mayer also traced the rivalry's flashpoint back to what happened in the build-up.

"We were always actually really cool, and the only thing that kind of triggered that rivalry was me getting in her face during the face-off," she said, suggesting Cameron may have "had all those words to say" about her "deep down".

Cameron, who admitted she had "genuinely respected" Mayer before the build-up soured, believes the hostility rebounded on the American.

"I was looking at her before the bell rang and thought, 'I'm going to smash your head in'," said Cameron after the fight. "And it worked. I was feeling the energy, she didn't want to be in there."

The contest exacted a toll befitting its billing, both fighters visibly swollen by the ninth round with Mayer cut by the eye and Cameron bleeding from hers, and the two embraced at the final bell before the verbal hostilities resumed.

A day on from disputing the verdict, Mayer struck a markedly different tone.

"I have not watched the fight back, but I am open to the idea that it was too close," she said. "I told myself I would not let the fight get close, and I didn't do that. I let it get too close, and so I can't be upset at the decision.

"It wasn't my night, and I have to give her the props for the win. She's a great fighter, and I'm just excited to go fix my mistakes and do better."

Victory further burnished a Cameron CV that already carried the only professional defeat inflicted on Katie Taylor, although the Briton played down talk of being the greatest of all time, insisting Claressa Shields still holds that mantle.

Rematch 'in the contract' with three-minute rounds on the table

Mayer confirmed a rematch clause exists and that she expects it to be activated.

The American also revealed she had declined to give up her WBC belt to make Saturday's fight three-minute rounds, and says the choice now rests with the new champion.

"I don't see a way that it doesn't happen because it's in the contract," she said. "We both want it and we'll make it happen.

"I wasn't willing to vacate my WBC belt in order to go three-minute rounds. In order to go three-minute rounds, I had to vacate that WBC belt but I know how much the belts play a role in your negotiation.

"She has the belts and she wants to go three-minute rounds. We can absolutely do that. I have no problem with that. It's her choice now, just like it was my choice for this fight."

Cameron made three-minute rounds her condition in the immediate aftermath of the dramatic victory.

"I want to do this again," she said on Saturday night. "It's up to Mikaela, but I want to do three-minute rounds."

Her coach Jamie Moore also said the champion could vacate the WBC belt if the sanctioning body refuses.

MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian welcomed a second meeting while revealing Cameron has pushed for fights with Claressa Shields and Lauren Price "from the jump".

He also insisted that the 35-year-old Brit is "unequivocally" among the top two or three female fighters of all time, if not the greatest.

Mayer, who on Saturday had insisted any rematch must happen in the United States, made no mention of venue and instead paid tribute to the UK fans.

"I love you guys, I can't wait to come back. I'm here for your entertainment," she added.
